newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - FX vols mostly lower, mark/lira bid.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FX vols mostly lower, mark/lira bid.

text.p: Implied volatilities for foreign exchange options were mostly lower in early afternoon trade on Friday, the notable exception being mark/lira.

Renewed speculation that the lira's re-entry into the European Union's exchange rate mechanism will be announced this weekend buoyed the currency against the German mark, driving short-dated volatility higher, over-the-counter (OTC) dealers said.
"The center of activity would be in the mark/lira options," said one OTC dealer with a Canadian bank. Otherwise, forex options activity was subdued ahead of the weekend.
Implied volatility for one-month at-the-money mark/lira options was 5.65/6.0 percent compared with 4.6/5.0 percent at the beginning of the week, he said.

Italy's Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said in Frankfurt that the Italian government would seek re-entry of the lira into the ERM in November. That sparked speculation that differences had receded between Italy and key EU partners France and Germany, and that re-entry could occur soon.
A European Union diplomat said a key committee would meet on Saturday to discuss Italy's request.
Another OTC dealer, with a U.S. bank, said most of the day's activity involved mark crosses.
"People are just trying to make plays around EMU," he said, noting increased interest in options on mark/lira, mark/French franc and mark/peseta.
Beyond that, trade was quiet, he said. Implied volatilities for both dollar/mark and dollar/yen options lost ground as the dollar rose above 1.50 marks and 111.50 yen.
Implied volatility for one-month dollar/mark options slid to 6.7/7.0 percent from 6.85/7.15 percent late Thursday.
Implied volatility for one-month dollar/yen dropped to 6.55/6.85 percent from 6.7/6.9 percent.
"We've seen a lot of people looking to sell volatilities as the dollar moves higher," the dealer said.
However, a dealer with a European bank said he did not believe the market was terribly concerned about dollar strength.
"On the short end, it's not like people are too concerned about the (dollar) upside," he said. "If it (a dollar rally) happens, they think it's going to be a slow move."
The second dealer said there was still room for dollar/mark and dollar/yen volatilities, which are near historic lows, to slide.

"It can go a lot lower," he said. "We get into these ranges through these holidays and, especially in the long end, you could see some really low volatilities -- the low six percents. But you'll start to see the curve flatten a lot too," he said.
